mainTopic: The essential parts of חליצה, who can perform it, whether a mute person's חליצה is valid, and the power of spitting alone
overview: The amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת from the previous משנה. רבי אליעזר says every action in חליצה, spitting included, is essential, while רבי עקיבא says only the action done on the man's body, taking off the shoe, is essential. A new משנה teaches that חליצה with a חרש, a חרשת or a minor boy is invalid, that a minor girl must repeat it when she grows up, and that a disqualified judge makes it invalid, though רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר disagree and רבי עקיבא once approved a private חליצה done in prison. In the גמרא, רבא first rules that a mute person's חליצה is valid because the reading is not essential. The teaching of the house of רבי ינאי knocks this out, so רבא's statement is moved to the חרש clause and reversed: a mute person's חליצה is invalid. The משנה is explained with רבי זירא's rule that something which can be done is not essential, but something which cannot be done at all is essential. Next comes a ruling sent to אבוה דשמואל that a יבמה who spat must do חליצה, which shows that spitting alone forbids her to the brothers. The גמרא rules out רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר as its source and ties it to רבי, using a ברייתא about the שבועות lambs. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to question whether רבי עקיבא really holds that spitting does not disqualify; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Every action in חליצה is essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from the words 'ככה יעשה' that any part of חליצה that is an action is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: 'So shall it be done' teaches that anything that is an action holds back the חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a source from the פסוק to show that every action in חליצה must be done, or the חליצה does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה said the reading is not essential, but whether spitting is essential was disputed. רבי אליעזר reads 'ככה' ('so') as 'exactly this way'. That makes every action essential, including spitting, while the words that are only recited are still not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So shall it be done' (דברים 25:9)
An action, as opposed to words that are recited
Holds back; essential, so without it the act is invalid
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from יבום

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
'So shall it be done'
any element that is an action is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous משנה's discussion of which parts of חליצה are essential.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any part of חליצה that is an action, spitting included, is essential.

steps.title: Only the action done on the man is essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי אליעזר's proof. The rest of the פסוק, 'לאיש', limits the essential part to an action done on the man's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Is that your proof? The פסוק says 'so shall it be done to the man', so only an action done on the man is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on רבי אליעזר's reading of the פסוק by pointing to the next word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק says 'so shall it be done to the man'. Taking off the shoe is done to the man's body, so it is essential. Spitting only happens in front of him, so it is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that a proof?', a way of rejecting someone's source
To the man
On the man, meaning done to his body

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that every action, spitting included, is essential. רבי עקיבא holds that only taking off the shoe, which is done on the man, is essential.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
Is that where you bring a proof from?
'So shall it be done to the man'
only an element that is an action done on the man.
phrases.notes: Taking off the shoe is done on his body. Spitting only happens in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by reading the next word of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's conclusion that every action is essential.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He did not read the word 'לאיש', which limits the rule to actions done on the man.

steps.title: Who cannot do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that חליצה is invalid when done by a deaf-mute man or woman, or with a minor boy. A minor girl must do חליצה again once she grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a deaf-mute man had חליצה done to him, or a deaf-mute woman did חליצה, or a woman did חליצה with a minor boy, her חליצה is invalid. If a minor girl did חליצה, she must do it again when she grows up. If she does not, her חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה lists people whose חליצה does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a חרש or a קטן makes the חליצה invalid. A minor girl's חליצה is not enough on its own, so she must repeat it as an adult. If she never repeats it, the first one does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute man or woman, who in הלכה is treated as lacking full understanding
A minor boy or girl
Once she grows up
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Here חרש does not just mean deaf. It means someone who can neither hear nor speak. The גמרא's argument later in this section depends on that.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute man who had חליצה done to him,
and a deaf-mute woman who did חליצה,
and a woman who does חליצה with a minor boy:
her חליצה is invalid.
A minor girl who did חליצה:
she must do חליצה again once she grows up,
and if she did not do it again,
her first חליצה is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that moves from the actions of חליצה to the people doing it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה done by a חרש, a חרשת, or with a קטן is invalid. A קטנה must repeat it as an adult.

steps.title: A judge who turns out to be disqualified
steps.stepSummary: If one of the judges is found to be a relative or disqualified, the חליצה is invalid. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did חליצה in front of two or three judges and one of them turned out to be a relative or disqualified, her חליצה is invalid. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the בית דין that sits for חליצה and records a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that the חליצה depends on having a fully valid בית דין, so one bad judge ruins it. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר hold that the חליצה still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who may not serve as a judge
They declare it valid

phrases.english: If she did חליצה in front of two or three judges,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל —
phrases.english: and one of them turned out to be a relative or disqualified:
her חליצה is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yochanan the sandal maker say it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a rule about the judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion says a disqualified judge makes the חליצה invalid. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר say it is valid.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא approves a private חליצה in prison
steps.stepSummary: A story: a man did חליצה alone with the woman in prison, and רבי עקיבא declared it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story of a man who did חליצה privately with her in prison. The case came before רבי עקיבא, and he declared it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real story that supports the lenient side, that חליצה can be valid even without a proper בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this story there was no proper panel of judges at all, yet רבי עקיבא allowed the חליצה after the fact. That backs up the lenient view of רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.

keyTerms.meaning: And there was a story, which is used to prove a ruling
Between him and her, privately
Prison

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends by bringing support for the lenient view: רבי עקיבא approved a חליצה done with no בית דין.

phrases.english: And there was a story of a certain man who did חליצה
privately, just him and her, in prison,
and the case came before Rabbi Akiva,
and he declared it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that supports the lenient opinion in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The lenient view that חליצה can be valid without a proper בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case judged by רבי עקיבא, who approved a private חליצה done in prison.

steps.title: A mute man or woman can do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא reasons that since the reading is not essential, a mute man or woman who did חליצה has a valid חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that you have said the reading does not hold back the חליצה, it follows that if a mute man or a mute woman did חליצה, their חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבא drawing a practical conclusion from the earlier rule that the reading is not essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mute person cannot say the פסוקים that are normally read at חליצה. Since the earlier משנה taught that missing the reading does not ruin the חליצה, רבא says a mute person's חליצה works.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of the פסוקים at חליצה
Does not hold it back; not essential
A mute man or woman who can hear but cannot speak
Valid

phrases.english: גמרא: Rava said:
Now that you have said
that the reading does not hold back the חליצה,
therefore, a mute man and a mute woman who did חליצה:
their חליצה is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a conclusion drawn from the earlier rule about the reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mute man or woman can do a valid חליצה, because the reading is not essential.

steps.title: Challenge from the חרש case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from our משנה: a חרש's חליצה is invalid, and that seems to be because he cannot do the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if a deaf-mute man had חליצה done, or a deaf-mute woman did חליצה, or a woman did חליצה with a minor, her חליצה is invalid. What is the reason? Isn't it because they cannot do the reading?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה to attack רבא's ruling about a mute person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חרש is invalid because he cannot speak the reading, then the reading would be essential after all. In that case a mute person, who also cannot speak, should be invalid too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
People able to do the reading

phrases.english: We learned: a deaf-mute man who had חליצה done to him,
and a deaf-mute woman who did חליצה,
and a woman who does חליצה with a minor boy:
her חליצה is invalid.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא בְּנֵי קְרִיָּיה נִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: Isn't it because they are not able to do the reading?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 6, using the משנה in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a mute person's חליצה is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חרש is invalid because he cannot read, then the reading is essential, and a mute person should be invalid too.

steps.title: A חרש is invalid because he lacks understanding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a חרש is invalid because he lacks understanding, not because he cannot speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because they lack understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by giving a different reason why a חרש cannot do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש is treated as lacking understanding, so his actions do not count in הלכה. A mute person has full understanding and only lacks speech. Since the reading is not essential, the mute person's חליצה stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: People with understanding, who have mental competence

steps.whatToRemember: On this first approach, a חרש is invalid for חליצה because he lacks understanding, so a mute person's חליצה stays valid. This does not last: steps 11-13 drop this version of רבא and rule that a mute person's חליצה is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו בְּנֵי דֵעָה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: No. It is because they lack understanding.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו בְּנֵי דֵעָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by giving a different reason for the משנה's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the משנה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חרש is invalid because he cannot speak the reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חרש is invalid because he lacks understanding, so רבא's ruling about a mute person still stands.

steps.title: Then a mute man and woman should also be invalid
steps.stepSummary: If a חרש is invalid because he lacks understanding, why not say the same about an אילם and אילמת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a mute man and a mute woman too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 8. If a חרש is invalid because he lacks understanding, then maybe a mute person should also be treated as lacking understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said a חרש is out because of his mind, not his mouth. The גמרא asks whether a mute person, who also cannot speak, belongs in the same group. If he did, רבא's ruling from Step 6 that an אילם's חליצה is valid would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
A mute man, who can hear but cannot speak
A mute woman

phrases.english: If so,
a mute man and a mute woman too!
phrases.notes: He means: they should also count as lacking understanding, so their חליצה should be invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a חרש is invalid only because he lacks understanding
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mute person also cannot speak, so maybe he too should be treated as lacking understanding. That would contradict רבא's ruling that an אילם's חליצה is valid.

steps.title: Mute people have full understanding; only their speech is missing
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that an אילם and אילמת have full understanding. Only their mouth is the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A mute man and woman are people of understanding; it is only their mouth that hurts them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. Mute people think and understand perfectly well; they just cannot talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא draws a line between a חרש, who is treated as lacking understanding, and an אילם, who has full understanding and only lacks speech. Since this approach holds that the reading is not essential, being unable to speak is not a problem. So the אילם stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: People with full understanding
Their mouth
Hurts; is the problem

phrases.english: Rava said:
A mute man and woman are people of understanding,
and it is just their mouth that hurts them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִלֵּם וְאִלֶּמֶת בְּנֵי דֵעָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: lacking understanding versus lacking only speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mute person might be grouped with a חרש as lacking understanding
steps.terutzMaskana: A mute person has full understanding, so on this approach he is valid for חליצה

steps.title: The house of רבי ינאי says a חרש is invalid because he cannot recite
steps.stepSummary: The house of רבי ינאי taught that a חרש is invalid because he cannot fulfill 'he says' and 'she says.' That means the reason is speech, not understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the house of רבי ינאי say: because he cannot do 'he says' and 'she says'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that directly contradicts Step 8. It says a חרש is invalid because he cannot speak the required words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 claimed a חרש is out because he lacks understanding. The house of רבי ינאי says the reason is that the פסוקים require speaking. If speaking is the issue, then an אילם, who cannot speak either, should also be invalid, and רבא's ruling is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the study hall of רבי ינאי
'And he shall say,' from the חליצה פסוקים
'And she shall say,' from the חליצה פסוקים

phrases.english: But didn't the house of Rabbi Yannai say:
because he is not able to fulfill 'he says' and 'she says'!
phrases.notes: דברים 25:8–9. The point is that a חרש is out because he can't say the words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Steps 8 and 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a חרש is invalid because of understanding and not speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says outright that the reason is the speaking requirement. That makes the reading essential and undermines רבא's ruling that an אילם is valid.

steps.title: רבא's statement really belongs to the later part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier version and says רבא's statement was actually said about the later part of the משנה. That part rules a חרש's חליצה invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבא's statement was said, it was said on the latter part: A deaf-mute man who had חליצה done, a deaf-mute woman who did חליצה, and a woman who does חליצה with a minor — her חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the earlier version of רבא's statement. It is setting up a new, corrected version, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the house of רבי ינאי shows a חרש is out because he cannot speak, the old version of רבא, which said the reading is not essential, cannot stand. The גמרא now attaches רבא's words to the clause about the חרש. That clause shows the reading does matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; dropping what was said before
The latter part of a משנה
A deaf-mute, treated by הלכה as lacking full understanding
A minor

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions of רבא! The first version (Step 6) said an אילם is valid. The corrected version (next step) says an אילם is invalid. The גמרא is replacing the first, not adding to it.

phrases.english: Rather, when Rava's statement was said,
it was said about the latter clause:
A deaf-mute man who underwent chalitza,
or a deaf-mute woman who performed chalitza,
or a woman who performs chalitza with a minor —
her chalitza is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אִתְּמַר דְּרָבָא אַסֵּיפָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 11 by moving רבא's statement to a different clause
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the statement to a different part of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was commenting on the clause that shows the reading is not essential
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was commenting on the clause that disqualifies a חרש, which shows the reading is essential

steps.title: Corrected רבא: since the reading is essential, mute people are invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that since the reading is essential, a mute man or woman who did חליצה has an invalid חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that you say the reading is essential, therefore a mute man and woman who did חליצה — their חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the corrected version of רבא's statement. It is the opposite of Step 6: a mute person cannot do a valid חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clause about the חרש, read as the house of רבי ינאי reads it, shows that being unable to recite disqualifies. A mute person also cannot recite. So he is invalid too, even though he has full understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of the חליצה פסוקים
Holds back; is essential, so without it the act is invalid
Therefore

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that you have said that the reading is essential,
therefore a mute man and woman who did chalitza —
their chalitza is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ קְרִיָּיה מְעַכְּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the corrected content of רבא's statement, placed on the clause cited in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the reading is essential for those unable to do it, a mute man or woman cannot perform a valid חליצה

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי זירא's rule about mixing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה seems to say both that the reading is not essential and that a חרש is invalid for not reading. This fits רבי זירא's rule: what can be done is not essential, but what cannot be done at all is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה follows רבי זירא, for רבי זירא said: Whatever is fit for mixing, mixing does not hold it back; and whatever is not fit for mixing, mixing holds it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles an apparent contradiction inside the משנה. Earlier the משנה treats חליצה without the reading as valid, yet here someone who cannot read is invalid. It does this by borrowing רבי זירא's rule about mixing a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מנחה, if the flour and oil could be mixed, it is still valid even if no one actually mixed them. If they could not be mixed, it is invalid. In the same way, a person who can recite is valid even if he skipped the reading. A person who is unable to recite at all, like a חרש or an אילם, is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing the oil into the flour of a מנחה
Fit; able to be done

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of רבי זירא is that what can be done does not hold up the מצוה if skipped, but what cannot be done at all does. So someone who can recite but did not is still valid. Someone unable to recite, like an אילם, is invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch out: 'essential' here does not mean the reading must actually be said. It means a person must be able to say it. Skipping it is fine; being unable to say it is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle of רבי זירא appears across ש״ס. It explains how one act can be optional for some people and disqualifying for others.

phrases.english: And our Mishnah follows Rabbi Zeira.
For Rabbi Zeira said:
Whatever is fit to be mixed —
phrases.notes: He's talking about a מנחה, a flour offering that is mixed with oil.

phrases.english: mixing is not essential for it.
And whatever is not fit to be mixed —
mixing is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה fits with רבא's corrected ruling in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general principle borrowed from another area of הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to contradict itself: the reading is not essential, yet a חרש is invalid for being unable to read
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading is not essential for someone who can do it, but it is essential for someone who cannot
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Following רבי זירא, the reading of חליצה does not hold up the act for someone able to recite. It does hold it up for someone unable to recite, so an אילם's חליצה is invalid.

steps.title: A ruling sent to שמואל's father about a יבמה who spat
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent to אבוה דשמואל: once a יבמה has spat, she must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a message to שמואל's father: a יבמה who spat must now do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that was sent to אבוה דשמואל. It says a יבמה who has already spat must go on to do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spitting is one of the parts of the חליצה ceremony. This ruling says that once she has spat, the path of יבום is closed. Now she must finish with חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent by message)
The father of שמואל
A widow who is waiting for יבום or חליצה from her late husband's brother
She spat (one part of the חליצה ceremony)
She must do חליצה

phrases.english: They sent to the father of Shmuel:
A yevama who spat must do chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the weight of spitting alone, after the earlier discussion about whether the reading is essential.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who spat must now do חליצה.

steps.title: Inference: spitting disqualifies her from the brothers
steps.stepSummary: From this ruling we learn that the spitting alone made her forbidden to do יבום with the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this we can learn that she has become disqualified from the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ruling. Spitting by itself has made her forbidden to marry any of the brothers through יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling did not say she may now marry outside the family. It only says she must do חליצה. So the spitting did not free her. But it did shut the door on יבום, which gives spitting real legal power.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we learn from this that
She became disqualified
The brothers of the dead husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This inference gives spitting real power on its own. That sets up the next question: which תנא would give spitting that much weight?

phrases.english: By implication, she has become disqualified from the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal implication from the ruling in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spitting alone disqualifies the יבמה from יבום with all the brothers.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this? Maybe רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא this ruling follows and suggests רבי עקיבא. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say it is רבי עקיבא's,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view the ruling matches. It tries out רבי עקיבא as an answer. This is a setup line for the challenge that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא holds that if she did not spit, the חליצה is still valid. So the גמרא checks whether a ruling that gives spitting so much power can fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is this?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? If you say it is Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה, where רבי עקיבא says the חליצה is valid even if she did not spit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the ruling and its inference fit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that spitting alone disqualifies the יבמה from the brothers.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows it cannot be רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The אימורים hold back the offering only when they exist. One might think spitting is the same: essential while the יבמה can still spit. Yet רבי עקיבא says spitting is not essential even then. So how could spitting alone disqualify her from the brothers?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now consider a case where the מצוה can still be done. Here you could compare spitting to the altar fats: when they are missing, they do not hold things back, but when they exist, they do. Even there, רבי עקיבא said spitting does not hold things back. So could spitting make her disqualified from the brothers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the ruling follows רבי עקיבא. It uses a קל וחומר: if he says spitting is not essential even when it could be done, it cannot be strong enough to disqualify her on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the אימורים, missing fats do not stop the meat from being eaten, but fats that exist must be burned first. By that model, spitting should be essential when the יבמה is there and able to spit. Yet רבי עקיבא still says it is not essential, so he gives spitting very little weight and cannot be the source of the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Now if even... (opens a קל וחומר)
In a case where the מצוה can still be done
Just like; it is the same as
The fat parts of an offering that are burned on the altar
They hold things back; they are essential

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אימורים comparison is רבי עקיבא's own view. It is the logic one 'could say' for treating spitting as essential, and רבי עקיבא does not accept it. That is what makes the קל וחומר work.

phrases.english: Now, if in a case where there is a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means the יבמה is still there and able to spit.

phrases.english: where one could say
it is just like the altar fats,
that when they are not there, they do not hold things back,
phrases.notes: If the fats were lost, the כהנים may still eat the meat once the blood has been sprinkled.

phrases.english: but when they are there, they do hold things back,
Rabbi Akiva said it does not hold things back,
so can she become disqualified from the brothers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion from step 17 that the ruling follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ruling (spitting disqualifies her from the brothers) follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: רבי עקיבא says spitting is not essential even when the אימורים model would make it essential. So he cannot hold that spitting alone has the power to disqualify her from יבום.

steps.title: Maybe the ruling follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting רבי עקיבא, the גמרא suggests the ruling follows רבי אלעזר instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, maybe it follows רבי אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new candidate, רבי אלעזר, as the source of the ruling. This line sets up a challenge that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר holds that spitting is essential to חליצה. Since he treats spitting as important, he seems like a good fit for a ruling that gives spitting real legal force.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather. It brings a new suggestion after the last one failed.

phrases.english: But rather, according to Rabbi Elazar?
phrases.notes: This is the same תנא as רבי אליעזר in step 1, who says every action, spitting included, is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new תנא after רבי עקיבא was ruled out in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could רבי אלעזר be the source of the ruling that spitting alone disqualifies her?

steps.title: Two permitting acts do nothing one without the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר cannot be the source. For him shoe-removal and spitting are two permitting acts, and one such act has no effect without the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are two permitting acts, and with two permitting acts, one does not raise the status without the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the רבי אלעזר suggestion. By his own rule, spitting alone should have no effect at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אלעזר requires both acts, they count as a pair of 'permitting acts.' The rule for such a pair is that one alone changes nothing. So spitting by itself should not forbid her to the brothers, which is the opposite of the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Two acts that together permit or complete something
One does not raise the status without the other
But look. It brings in a challenge.

steps.confusionAlert: Calling spitting 'essential' does not make it stronger alone. For רבי אלעזר, being one of two essential acts means it does nothing until the other act is done too.

phrases.english: But they are two permitting acts,
phrases.notes: He means removing the shoe and spitting, which רבי אלעזר says are both needed.

phrases.english: and with two permitting acts,
one does not raise the status without the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggestion from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ruling follows רבי אלעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By his own rule, one of two permitting acts has no effect alone, so spitting alone could not disqualify her.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבי, as shown by the שבועות lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the ruling follows רבי. It brings a ברייתא that the שבועות lambs make the loaves holy only through their slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי. As it is taught: the lambs of עצרת make the bread holy only through slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the ruling follows רבי. It begins quoting a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the שבועות offering, the lambs are what make the accompanying loaves holy. The ברייתא says this happens at the slaughter. That opens the door to one act, the slaughter, having an effect before the second act, the sprinkling of the blood, is done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: The two lambs brought on שבועות along with the two loaves
Make the loaves holy
Slaughter of the animal

phrases.english: Rather, it follows Rabbi.
As it is taught: the lambs of Atzeret
make the bread holy only through slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two rejected candidates, gives the final answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows רבי, who lets one of two permitting acts have a partial effect alone.

steps.title: Proper slaughter alone makes the loaves partly holy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lays out three cases. If only the slaughter is done properly, the loaves are 'holy and not holy.' That shows one of two acts has some effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he slaughtered them for their sake and sprinkled their blood for their sake, the bread is holy. If he slaughtered not for their sake and sprinkled for their sake, the bread is not holy. If he slaughtered them for their sake and sprinkled their blood not for their sake, it is holy and not holy. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains its rule through three cases. In the last case, proper slaughter alone gives the loaves a partial holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughter and sprinkling are two permitting acts. Yet for רבי, the proper slaughter alone already has an effect on the loaves. In the same way, spitting alone can have an effect on the יבמה and forbid her to the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: For their own sake, meaning as the שבועות offering they are meant to be
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Holy and not holy, a partial holiness

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, one of two needed acts can create a partial status by itself. That is why the ruling about spitting follows רבי and not רבי עקיבא or רבי אלעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It lets the גמרא tie the ruling sent to אבוה דשמואל to a known opinion. Through the link to קדשים, spitting alone can change the יבמה's status.

phrases.english: How so? If he slaughtered them for their sake,
and sprinkled their blood for their sake, the bread is holy.
If he slaughtered not for their sake, and sprinkled for their sake,
the bread is not holy.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחָטָן לִשְׁמָן, וְזָרַק דָּמָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן —
phrases.english: If he slaughtered them for their sake, and sprinkled their blood not for their sake,
it is holy and not holy. These are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: The loaves are holy enough that they can't be redeemed, but not holy enough to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 21 and shows the key case.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי lets one of two permitting acts have an effect alone
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the שבועות lambs, in the case of proper slaughter with improper sprinkling

steps.title: The opposing view: both acts are needed for the loaves to become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds the loaves become holy only when both the slaughter and the blood-throwing are done for the sake of the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the loaves never become holy unless he slaughters the lambs for their proper purpose and also throws their blood for their proper purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a dissenting opinion: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says one act alone does nothing. Both acts must be done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His view is the opposite of the earlier view in the ברייתא, which said one proper act makes the loaves 'holy and not holy.' Because he disagrees, we can see that the earlier view really is a separate opinion: one of two acts does have some effect. That is the view step 21 tied to רבי, and it matches the idea that spitting alone can disqualify the יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: 'never,' in no case
For their own sake, for the offering's proper purpose
Throwing the blood on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions in this ברייתא match the two possible readings of spitting in חליצה: one act alone has some effect, or it has none at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
It never becomes holy
phrases.notes: 'It' means the שבועות loaves from the ברייתא in step 21.

phrases.english: unless he slaughters them for their own sake
and throws their blood for their own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in steps 21-22 by quoting the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling about spitting follows the view that one of two acts has some effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the שבועות loaves. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's demand for both acts shows the earlier view is a real separate opinion.

steps.title: Does רבי עקיבא really hold that spitting does not disqualify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions its earlier assumption about רבי עקיבא and starts quoting a ברייתא that seems to contradict it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רבי עקיבא really say that spitting does not disqualify her? Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: if she removed the shoe but did not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to steps 17-18, where it said רבי עקיבא holds spitting is not essential. Now it challenges that claim and starts to bring a ברייתא as evidence. The quote continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא rejected רבי עקיבא as the source of the ruling, because it thought he holds spitting does nothing. Now it attacks that very assumption. If a ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא does hold that spitting disqualifies, the earlier rejection falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But did he really say?', a formula that questions an assumed view
Spitting, one of the acts of חליצה
Disqualifies her from marrying a brother through יבום
She removed the brother's shoe (did חליצה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is questioning its own earlier claim about רבי עקיבא from step 18, not the ruling about the loaves.

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Akiva say
that spitting does not disqualify?
phrases.notes: Disqualify her from later marrying one of the other brothers through יבום.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
If she removed the shoe but did not

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רְקִיקָה לָא פָּסְלָה וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier rejection of רבי עקיבא and challenges what it assumed about his view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption from step 18 that רבי עקיבא holds spitting does not disqualify the יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא seems to attribute to רבי עקיבא the view that spitting does affect her status, which contradicts the assumption.
